title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 236 (Person falsely contracting as agent not entitled to performance)

content.overview: Section 236 provides that a person with whom a contract has been entered into in the character of agent is not entitled to require the performance of it, if he was in reality acting, not as agent, but on his own account.
content.glance: One who contracted as agent but was really acting on own account cannot require performance of that contract.
content.study: Where a contract is entered into with a person in the character of agent, and that person was in reality acting not as agent but on his own account, he is not entitled to require performance of the contract. The section prevents a person from claiming contractual performance in a capacity different from the one in which the contract was made. Current-law framing: identify the character in which the contract was entered; test whether the person was in reality acting on own account; conclude no right to require performance.

sections.heading: Contract in character of agent
sections.body: The contract was entered into with a person in the character of agent.

sections.heading: Reality — acting on own account
sections.body: That person was in reality acting not as agent but on his own account.

sections.heading: Consequence
sections.body: He is not entitled to require performance of the contract.

provisions.title: Person falsely contracting as agent, not entitled to performance

examples.title: Own-account dealing under agent character
examples.body: A contracts with B representing himself as C’s agent, but A is dealing for his own benefit. A cannot require B to perform the contract for A’s benefit.

hypotheticals.question: Can a person who posed as agent later enforce the contract for himself?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 236 bars requiring performance where the person contracted in the character of agent but was in reality acting on own account.

distinctions.title: False agent not entitled to performance (s. 236) vs liability of pretended agent (s. 235)
distinctions.left: Bars the false agent from requiring performance
distinctions.right: Compels the pretended agent to compensate the third person

misconceptions.trap: Anyone who contracts can always enforce it regardless of the character assumed.
misconceptions.correction: Section 236 denies performance to a person who contracted as agent but was really acting on own account.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 236 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify the character in which the contract was made. II. Test whether the person was really acting on own account. III. Conclude no right to require performance.
